note: Regime A path green after two fixes: (1) blocked chain outputs need ReservePolicy/PushPolicy::PerBlockSize (PerTile emits ONE reserve+push per BLOCK, not per tile -> writer hang); (2) sum_of_squares only accumulates tiles element-wise, so Regime A needs a within-tile reduce<SUM,REDUCE_ROW> finalize (accumulate-then-finalize).

Regime B multi-chunk corrupts specific tiles deterministically (bad tiles 304,305,308,309,508,509 for (1,1,32,16384)). Diagnosis: a multi-page cb_reserve_back/cb_wait_front + contiguous N-page access is only legal when the CB page count is a multiple of N and the fifo pointer is N-aligned. Two sources of misalignment: (a) a W-chunk tail whose width differs from the block (Wt not divisible by the chunk), (b) a partial last row-block (ht < BLOCK_HT). Both leave the fifo pointer off-grid so the next full-size access runs past the CB end into the neighbouring CB. Fix: chunk must DIVIDE Wt_core (no tail) and row-blocks are always exactly BLOCK_HT tile-rows (reader clamps phantom tile-rows to the last valid one; the writer emits only valid rows).
Green in both default and --dev mode after the CB-wrap fix (divisor W-chunks + full BLOCK_HT row-blocks with phantom-row clamp).

what: The doc covers push/pop balance and intermediate-CB sizing but never states the CB FIFO WRAP invariant: a multi-page cb_reserve_back/cb_wait_front followed by a CONTIGUOUS N-page access (get_write_ptr + N*page_size) is only legal when the CB page count is a multiple of N AND the fifo pointer is N-aligned. Violating it writes past the end of the CB into the neighbouring one - no hang, no assert, just deterministic corruption of a few tiles. This cost the largest debugging block of the run: a short trailing W-chunk and a partial last row-block each left the pointer off-grid. The rule is only visible indirectly, as ASSERT(num_pages % tiles_per_bulk == 0) buried in reduce_helpers_compute.inl.
suggest: Add a CB-wrap section next to the sync invariant: state the rule, give the two ways to satisfy it (every multi-page access is a fixed size that divides the page count, or reserve/push one page at a time), and name the silent-corruption failure mode so it is greppable.

what: ReservePolicy/PushPolicy::PerTile reads as per-tile, and the PerBlockSize doc ('synchronizes a CB once per IterationShape::block_size group') reinforces that. Under a blocked walk it is actually per OUTER ITERATION: chain.inl emits one cb_reserve_back(1)/cb_push_back(1) per block, so grid(Ht,Wt).block_size(4) packs 4 tiles into 1 CB page and pushes 1 - silent wrong data plus a consumer hang. PerBlockSize is the only correct pack-output policy for a blocked chain.
suggest: State on the ReservePolicy/PushPolicy enums that PerTile means per outer iteration (== per tile only when block_size==1), and add a static_assert or doc line: a chain with block_size>1 must use PerBlockSize on its pack output.

what: The doc documents ttnn.div_up, ttnn.round_up and ttnn.find_max_divisor with worked examples and a summary table; none of the three exist in this tree (AttributeError on first use). It also has no entry for querying per-core L1 size, which every budget solver needs - the real API is ttnn.get_max_worker_l1_unreserved_size() (module-level, no device arg); device.l1_size_per_core() does not exist on MeshDevice.
suggest: Re-verify the bindings list against the tree; drop or mark-unavailable the three missing helpers, and add ttnn.get_max_worker_l1_unreserved_size() to the Summary Table as the L1-budget query.

what: The prompt (and .claude/references/ttnn-python-utility-bindings.md:34, 'rounded up to DRAM alignment of 32') states 32-byte DRAM alignment. On Blackhole ttnn.get_dram_alignment() returns 64. A gamma ingest path built on the 32 B assumption tripped the watcher with 'invalid address alignment in NOC transaction' on a read whose source was 32 B-aligned but not 64 B-aligned, and had to be redesigned.
suggest: Replace the hardcoded 32 with 'query ttnn.get_dram_alignment() - 64 on Blackhole, 32 on Wormhole' in both places, and note that a read at an OFFSET INTO a page must satisfy that alignment, not just the page base.

what: The design maps sum_of_squares straight onto cb_sumsq and declares its 'Valid region: Col0', i.e. it treats the helper as producing a finished REDUCE_ROW result. It does not: sum_of_squares accumulates x*x across a tile-ROW element-wise into one full 32x32 tile, so column c holds the sum over all W-tiles at column c. A within-tile reduce<SUM,REDUCE_ROW> finalize is still required, which also means Regime A needs the bf16 scaler CB the design gives only to Regime B. Cost a full debug cycle - output was off by exactly a factor of sqrt(Wt).
suggest: In convenience.hpp say explicitly that sum_of_squares emits a TILE-accumulated result, not a row-reduced one, and that it pairs with a reduce<SUM,REDUCE_ROW> finalize; designs citing it should carry that second step and its scaler CB.

what: The prompt says the background C++ build failed and to run ./build_metal.sh. Running it still fails - on unrelated C++ TEST targets that include the nuked ops (test_softmax_op.cpp, test_layernorm_op.cpp, test_conv2d.cpp) - and ninja stops before the python extension is usable, so 'import ttnn' fails with ModuleNotFoundError: ttnn._ttnn. The library itself builds fine; the .so just never gets linked into ttnn/ttnn/. Recovering this cost real time before any op work could start.
suggest: In the eval harness build step either build the library targets only (ninja ttnn/_ttnn.so ttnn/_ttnncpp.so) or nuke the C++ gtest sources alongside the op sources; and tell the agent that ttnn/ttnn/_ttnn.so + _ttnncpp.so must be symlinked from build/ttnn/ for the editable install to import.

detail: bf8b PCC>=0.99989, bf16+acc=False PCC>=0.99999 — both new axis values work first try with the derived interm/acc CB formats
81 passed — prior-phase regression net green after the SUPPORTED widening

162 passed / 10 failed / 200 xfailed. ALL bf8b cells pass. The 10 failures are wide-W bf16 loose cases at fp32_dest_acc_en=False: PCC 0.99993-0.99996 (above the 0.9995 gate) but harness rms 0.0405-0.126 > dtype-keyed target 0.04. rms grows monotonically with W (5120->0.0405, 7168->0.0514, 11008->0.126) => bf16 DEST accumulator precision over a wide reduction, not a structural bug.

hypothesis: The wide-W rms miss at fp32_dest_acc_en=False is sum-of-squares accumulator loss. Two candidate sites: (a) the cross-chunk running sum parked in cb_sumsq (which acc_narrow=1 just narrowed to bf16), (b) the within-chunk tile accumulation in bf16 DEST. The acc_narrow=0 off-arm isolates (a): if fp32 acc CBs recover the rms, the loss is at the chunk boundary and the fix is to keep the accumulator CBs fp32 regardless of DEST width.

detail: wr sweep 112->2 (2..112 chunks) x acc CB {fp32,bf16} at fp32_dest_acc_en=False gives BIT-IDENTICAL rms (0.05138 at W=7168, 0.12038 at W=11008). Hypothesis REFUTED: the sum-of-squares accumulation depth is not the loss site — if it were, changing the checkpoint frequency would change the rounding pattern. Also proves acc_narrow costs zero precision at any depth.

ROOT CAUSE. Matched-width A-vs-B comparison (W=1016/1024, 2040/2048, 4088/4096 force B vs A at identical Wt): Regime A at fp32_dest_acc_en=False is CLEAN (scale bias -0.0009..+0.0006, better than A at fp32-on); Regime B is biased and grows with TOTAL Wt: sumsq +0.84% (Wt=32), +1.90% (64), +5.56% (128), +10.37% (224). Independent of gamma value/dtype, math_fidelity, DEST_BLOCK, W-chunk size and acc-CB format. => reduce_tile’s long DEST accumulation at 16-bit DEST; Regime A’s element-wise/pairwise accumulate is unaffected. My earlier no-gamma control at W=7168 was Regime A, not B — that is what made it look gamma-related.

hypothesis: Switching Regime B’s reduce to ReduceAlgorithm::AccumulateViaAdd (pairwise FPU add_tiles into one DST + SFPU within-tile finalize on the last chunk) removes the bias, because it is the same accumulate shape Regime A already proves clean at 16-bit DEST. The helper documents it as SUM-only, BulkWaitBulkPop-with-Accumulate, partial-scaler-composable, and more accurate for wide reduces.

fix: Regime B reduce datapath -> ReduceAlgorithm::AccumulateViaAdd (+ BulkWaitBulkPop, + Accumulate::at_last on the finalizing chunk), as CT arg 22 off blocking_plan.reduce_via_add with lever reduce_via_add (off-arm = the Phase-0 ReduceTile path).
result: CONFIRMED. fp32_dest_acc_en=False rms is now 0.0061-0.0088 and FLAT in W (Wt 32..344); previously 0.0086 -> 0.1219 growing with W. At fp32_dest_acc_en=True both datapaths agree (0.0078-0.0101 vs 0.0072-0.0086). All widths now under the 0.04 bf16 gate.

fix: Reader emits the partial form matching the datapath (prepare_reduce_mask 0/1 row-0-broadcast mask for AccumulateViaAdd, prepare_partial_reduce_scalers for ReduceTile) and compute passes ReducePartialScaler::partial_mask(W_PARTIAL,1) vs last_tile_at(1), both off the single REDUCE_VIA_ADD knob.
result: golden slice 172 passed / 0 failed (was 10 wide-W failures before the datapath fix, then 6 w_non_aligned pad-poison failures from passing the ReduceTile partial form to AccumulateViaAdd — last_tile_at carries only a scaler index, so valid_reduce_dim_elements stayed 0 and the datapath never masked).

test: eval/golden_tests/rms_norm/test_golden.py -k (False or BFLOAT8_B) and INTERLEAVED and not loose
detail: 792 passed / 8 failed / 420 xfailed. Every fp32_dest_acc_en=False cell and every bf8b-INPUT cell passes. The 8 failures are ONE signature: dtype=FLOAT32 x gamma_dtype=BFLOAT8_B x w_non_aligned (i.e. Regime B), rms 0.10-0.63 vs the fp32 target 0.02. The same bf8b gamma with a bf16 input passes, and fp32 x bf8b-gamma on tile_aligned (Regime A) passes — so it is not plain gamma quantization.

REGRESSION FOUND (and my slice had deselected it): the 8 failures are NOT gamma-related — bf8b and bf16 gamma give identical errors. The real condition is via_add=1 + FLOAT32 input + w_non_aligned: rms 0.592/0.112 at via_add=1 vs 0.0011/0.0011 at via_add=0. Cause: AccumulateViaAdd folds the partial MASK tile out of the scaler CB (mandatory bfloat16) with no data-format reconfig, so a float32 cb_squared makes the datapath unpack the bf16 mask as float32. bf16/bf8b inputs are clean because their cb_squared is already bfloat16.

fix: Gate AccumulateViaAdd on NEEDED (16-bit DEST, where ReduceTile carries the width-growing bias) AND CORRECT (the scaler CB is mandatorily bfloat16 and the datapath folds the mask out of it with no reconfig, so a masked reduce needs interm_dtype == bfloat16, or no mask at all).
result: Full precision matrix (7 widths x 3 in-dtypes x 3 gamma-dtypes x 2 DEST widths) has ZERO cells outside their dtype tolerance. Golden slice incl. the previously-deselected fp32 w_non_aligned cells: 436 passed / 0 failed.
